notes:
Gold standard A: statute cross-references and defined terms, labelled by careful reading of each section's full text (lexflow.ask.index.text_of). Sections: every .xref_sample.json entry for va, dc, md and tx (33: dc 8, md 8, tx 8, va 9; Va. Code Ann. § 54.1-204 included). Totals: 360 references (285 resolvable in the index, 75 not; 22 generic) and 89 terms (27 with a definition span; 40 with a Wikidata link). References by kind: {'internal_relative': 89, 'pinpoint': 68, 'list_item': 64, 'other_code': 53, 'section': 51, 'container': 10, 'named_act': 9, 'federal': 6, 'regulation': 5, 'court_rule': 3, 'constitution': 1, 'range': 1}. By role: {'scope': 110, 'condition': 67, 'prerequisite_process': 44, 'authority': 44, 'procedure': 41, 'exception': 26, 'definition': 11, 'other': 9, 'penalty': 5, 'override': 3}. Terms by kind: {'role/actor': 41, 'document': 14, 'thing': 12, 'process': 10, 'status': 8, 'other': 4}.

SPANS. 'span' is the exact text of I.text_of(state, id), and 'start'/'end' are character offsets into it (the builder located each span in reading order and verified it; MD section numbers keep the source's en dash, e.g. '§ 7–504.1', and D.C. § 2-1402.66 has a thin space U+2009 after '§'). Each occurrence is its own reference, repeats included.

TARGETS. target_sections holds full index citations, each verified with I.lookup(state, citation): every returned row has exactly that citation. target_ids are the matching index row ids. A self-reference ('this section', 'subsection B', Texas CCP 'this article', which there means the section) targets the section's own citation, with 'pinpoint' set when narrower. Containers and 'this chapter/subtitle/title/subchapter' have target_sections null (or an 'et seq.' anchor section when the text names one) and a target_unit: label; index_path; exact (whether the index has that unit as a path level); anchor; range with range_basis ('text' = boundaries stated in the code's own text, 'numbering' = inferred from the Texas section-numbering convention); and index_sections (row count under index_path). Index paths stop at the chapter in D.C. and Texas (no subchapters) and at the subtitle in Maryland (no Parts). resolvable_in_index is true when target_sections verify, or when target_unit is an exact path level with rows, or when a range is verified from the text (Md. CP Title 11, Subtitle 6, Part I = §§ 11-601 to 11-619, since § 11-621 opens Part II). It is false for federal law, generic references, repealed or missing sections, and units the paths cannot express, even when a numbering range is given.

KIND precedence, when several apply: federal > constitution > court_rule > regulation > named_act > other_code > range > list_item > pinpoint > container > internal_relative > section. A pinpoint into another code is therefore kind other_code, with 'pinpoint' filled; items of a list in another code are other_code with a shared list_group. LISTS: each item is its own reference, with list_group numbered within the section; the list's shared trailing qualifier ('of this chapter', ', Penal Code', 'of this article') belongs to the last item's span. RANGES are one reference with target_sections expanded. generic=true marks a reference to a category of law that names no provision (federal requirements, board regulations, the Mayor's rules, court rules, other jurisdictions' statutes, local ordinances, the State budget); scorers may exclude these. repealed=true marks a repealed target.

ROLE conventions. 'subject to', if-clauses and criteria to be met -> condition. Enumerations of the offenses or items a rule covers, and self-references that bound coverage ('under this section') -> scope. A status or document produced by another procedure ('referred for collections pursuant to', 'entered into a payment plan under', 'a determination made under', 'notice issued under', 'licensed under this chapter', 'an affirmative finding under') -> prerequisite_process. 'as defined in', 'has the meaning assigned by', 'described by', and an entity identified by the section that creates it ('Fund established under § 3-306') -> definition. 'authorized by', 'adopted pursuant to', 'regulations adopted under', 'acts under' -> authority. 'in accordance with' or 'as provided in' a procedure -> procedure. 'does not apply' and 'except as provided' -> exception. 'notwithstanding' -> override.

EXCLUDED, deliberately: Virginia legislative-history lines ('Code 1950, § 19.1-341.2; 1960, c. 366; ...'); Maryland section-number labels ('§10–105.2.'); bare-'law' phrases ('contrary to law', 'or other law', 'allowed by law', 'established under law', 'required by law', 'in accordance with law', 'state law or a local ordinance'); grants of rulemaking power ('to promulgate regulations'); case-law doctrine (D.C. § 2-510 'rules of law which define the scope and limitations of review', 'rule of prejudicial error'); and agency guidelines or procedures ('guidelines promulgated by the Office of the Attorney General', 'procedures established by the Department of Taxation'). Included as a reference: the editorial session-law note 'CHAPTER 95 OF 2025' (Md. CP § 10-401).

TERMS. 'how' is one of: means, means_and_includes, shall_contain, meaning_assigned, as_defined_in, parenthetical ('(“University”)'), condition ('Restitution is overdue if ...'), criteria (§ 54.1-204's 'directly relates' test), is, establishes ('There is established ...'), heading (a role, document, program or process the heading names, after the 'Incorporators.' convention, which comes from lexipedia.wikibase.cloud Item:Q168 = Fla. Stat. § 607.0201 'Incorporators.', outside this set), quoted_mention ('good moral character'), used_defined_elsewhere (a term the section only uses, defined in the governing definitions section named in defined_in), and used. 'definition' is the exact defining span, with offsets, or null. 'scope' is the unit the definition governs. 'source' is text, heading, or heading+text. defined_in is a verified index citation. 'wikidata' is a hand-checked wikidata.org item ({id, label, description, match}): exact = the same specific entity, concept = the same general concept, close = a near-synonym in another vocabulary, broader = a parent concept. null means no defensible match: state-specific actors such as 'Board', 'Division' and 'COST' had none.

RESOLVER TRAPS AND INDEX GAPS found while labelling: (1) Md. Code, Criminal Procedure §§ 10-101 and 10-105 are not in the index (§ 10-105.2 cites § 10-105 twice); a bare '10-105' lookup returns 18 sections of other articles. (2) Tex. Code Crim. Proc. art. 42.032 is not in the index; a bare '42.032' lookup returns only Tex. Election Code § 42.032, which retrieve.cited()'s fallback 'hits if len(hits) == 1' would wrongly accept. (3) Not in the index: D.C. Code § 47-2829, § 38-105 [repealed], and Title 3 Chapters 5, 36 and 37; Va. 'former § 18.2-250.1' (repealed). (4) Md. Transp. § 26-204(e)(3)(iii) cites '§ 5–504.1 of the Courts Article', which is not in the index; its parallel clauses cite § 7-504.1, so it is probably a codification error. (5) An article-qualified lookup is a substring match: I.lookup('tx', 'Government Code § 501.001') also returns Local Government Code § 501.001, so verify with full citations. (6) 'this article' means the Transportation Article (a code) in Maryland but the section itself in the Texas Code of Criminal Procedure; Maryland's 'Courts Article' is the Courts and Judicial Proceedings article. (7) Maryland text uses en dashes in section numbers; the index citations use hyphens.
